_note: THE SCREEN'S WORDS, in one place, read by every gate that judges copy: the Python reader is tests/gates/vocabulary.py, the client reader is frontend/scripts/lib/vocabulary.js.
Not to be confused with src/sift/kernel/vocabulary.py, which holds the closed lists of words the RECORD is stored in (identifiers, never shown). This file is what a person reads.

A pattern is a regular expression in the subset Python and JavaScript agree on: word boundaries, groups, classes, fixed-width lookarounds. Matched case-insensitively unless the entry says "case": true. Every pattern entry carries an "example" it MUST match; both readers prove every example, so a pattern that stops matching, or reads differently on the two sides, fails a test instead of passing a tree.

Two kinds of list. HARD lists (wrong_words, scoped_wrong_words, banned_everywhere) are zero today and stay zero. RATCHETED lists (retired_words, insider_phrases, contractions, phrasing, the verb allow-list) are counted per file against a recorded baseline that may only fall: frontend/scripts/gate-baselines.json for the client, tests/gates/data/copy_vocabulary_baseline.json for the server. spelling was a ratchet and is now held at zero on both sides, with nothing recorded.

contractions: Sift writes the way a person talks, so the screen says can't, don't, isn't, it's where a person would. Each entry is the uncontracted form, and instead names the contraction; each is case-sensitive with its first letter either way, so a query's IS NOT NULL is never read as words. Never shan't, and never 'd for would. it is / that is / there is are counted only where they can be contracted: not before not (that is the is not entry), not before punctuation or the end of a sentence, not before a closing word such as in, here or now (the folder it is in.), and it is not after a preposition, where it is the object (Everything in it is filed). The ratchet allows what remains on purpose: cannot in a legal or security statement of impossibility, and a warning an admin reads that opens with It is. A History line is not read by this list: its words follow the History word table.
Adding an entry: a word goes in when it has shipped, not when it can be imagined. Say what replaces it and give an example of the real sentence.

allowed_sentences._why: Sentences where a wrong word is right. A phrase rather than a file, so an exemption covers the sentence somebody argued for. Both are the stash-box connections pane saying how a box files its entries: the one place whose SUBJECT is somebody else's vocabulary. The two Remove sentences say taking a name off a face (the name leaves the face, which is membership, so Remove is the verb; Delete stays the word where a face ceases to exist); the second is the reader's spelling of the sentence with the name filled in.

banned_everywhere._why: Read by tests/gates/test_banned_words.py over every tracked file, comments included. _typography_why: Read by both copy gates (frontend/scripts/lib/vocabulary.js and tests/gates/vocabulary.py), each holding it at zero: three full stops where the ellipsis character belongs, and an arrow typed as "->", "<-" or "=>" where the arrow character belongs. Write \u2026 in a script string and … in markup.
_paths_why: A place in Sift is named by its breadcrumb, the screen and then each step, joined by " > ": Settings > Importing > Folders. On screen it is written plain; in a document or the changelog it is written in code ticks (tests/gates/test_paths_are_breadcrumbs.py). Every other way of naming a place is held at zero here.
